/speckit-specify This repository already contains `bookmarks`, a command-line bookmark manager that stores bookmarks in SQLite. Read the existing code and any documentation in the repository before changing it. Add the two features below; every existing command must keep working exactly as it does now. 1. **Import.** `python -m bookmarks [--db PATH] import FILE --format csv|json` reads bookmarks from FILE in the same formats that `export` writes: CSV with the header row `id,url,title,tags`, or a JSON array of objects with the keys `url`, `title` and `tags` (a list of strings). Each bookmark in the file is added exactly as the `add` command would add it, with the same rules for URLs, titles and tags. The `id` in the file is ignored, and new ids are assigned as usual. When it finishes it prints `imported N` to standard output, where N is the number of bookmarks added. If FILE cannot be read, or is not valid CSV or JSON of that shape, it prints an error message to standard error, imports nothing, and exits with status 2. 2. **HTML export.** `export --format html` prints all bookmarks, ordered by id, as an HTML page in this form: ``` Bookmarks
  • TITLE TAGS
``` with one `
  • ` line per bookmark, where TAGS are the bookmark's tags joined with commas in alphabetical order. Examples, with a file `in.json` containing `[{"url": "https://docs.python.org", "title": "Python docs", "tags": ["python", "docs"]}, {"url": "https://example.com", "title": "Example", "tags": []}]` and an empty database (`` stands for a tab character): ``` $ python -m bookmarks --db b.db import in.json --format json imported 2 $ python -m bookmarks --db b.db list 1https://docs.python.orgPython docsdocs,python 2https://example.comExample $ python -m bookmarks --db b.db export --format html (an HTML page that contains Python docs) ```

What the spec says, grounded in the existing code (`src/bookmarks/cli.py`, `store.py`), the feature-001 CLI contract and the constitution:

- **3 user stories** — import (P1), HTML export (P2), export→import round trip (P3) — each independently testable, plus 20 functional requirements (FR-001…FR-020) and 7 success criteria. Prior-feature requirements are cross-referenced as `001:FR-nnn` so numbering can't collide.

- **Preserved behaviour** is a requirement in its own right (FR-015…FR-018): same bytes, same statuses, no schema change, exit-status map extended not redefined.

Three judgment calls I made rather than blocking on — all in the spec's Assumptions and flagged in the checklist notes:

1. A failed import is **all-or-nothing**, including when one record's URL fails the `http(s)://` check — the whole import exits 2 and adds nothing (your "imports nothing" plus constitution Principle II, which forbids skipping bad records).
2. Import-**file** problems are status **2**; status **1** stays reserved for the store. The file is read and validated before the store is opened, so a failed import also creates no store file.
3. The HTML export **escapes** `&`, `<`, `>` (and `"` in `href`) from stored values, so an odd title still yields a well-formed page. Your example output is unchanged by this.
